c.tagline: Adriatic beach capital of Fellini, Roman ruins, and endless nightlife.

taxi.fareNote: White taxis queue at the station and along the seafront rather than being hailed on the street; fares are metered with surcharges at night and in high summer, so agree the approximate cost for longer runs.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance; 113 reaches state police and 118 reaches medical emergencies directly.

avoid.reason: Pickpockets work the beachfront promenade and the station area in summer, and the Marina Centro club strip gets rowdy late at night.

hood_desc: The inland old town around Piazza Cavour, the Renaissance Tempio Malatestiano, the Roman Arch of Augustus, and the Tiberius Bridge, plus Fellini's rejuvenated Cinema Fulgor; best for first-timers who want history and character away from the beach crowds.

The heart of the seaside resort: the grand belle-epoque Grand Hotel (Fellini's muse), the long Lungomare promenade, beach clubs, restaurants, and the busiest stretch of sand; the classic base for a lively beach-and-nightlife stay.

The colourful former fishermen's quarter across the Tiberius Bridge, a maze of low pastel houses covered in murals celebrating Fellini and his films; an arty, atmospheric spot for aperitivi and dinner by the old harbour canal.

A southern beachfront district by the airport and the Marano canal, known for family hotels, a long sandy beach, and the Parco del Mare seafront redevelopment; suits families and travellers wanting a calmer resort base.
A relaxed northern seaside frazione of family-run hotels, a wide beach, and a small marina; good for budget-minded and family travellers after a quieter, more local Riviera feel.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though many Italians prefer bottled for taste.

transit.pay: Buy tickets from tabaccherie, machines, the Roger app, or on board; a single urban ticket is about €1.50, with day and tourist passes sold in summer. Validate your ticket on boarding.
transit.hours: Start Romagna buses and the Metromare rapid-transit line run roughly 5:30am to midnight, busiest and most frequent along the coast in summer; taxis and ride apps cover the small hours.
transit.note: The Metromare bus-rapid-transit line links Rimini's station to Riccione along the coast; Start Romagna buses cover the city and the beach frazioni, and the flat seafront makes cycling popular.

transit.m: Metromare BRT / bus line 9 to Rimini station and seafront (~20 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a cover charge (coperto) is often already on the bill, so rounding up or leaving a few euros for good service is appreciated but not expected.

food.name: Piadina romagnola
food.desc: Thin unleavened flatbread cooked on a hot testo and folded around squacquerone cheese, rocket and prosciutto crudo.

places.name: Nud e Crud
places.note: Rimini-born piadineria that treats the flatbread seriously, with quality Romagnolo fillings.

places.name: Lungomare piadina kiosks
places.note: The classic seafront chioschi; a piadina eaten walking the promenade is the local habit.

places.name: Mercato Coperto
places.note: Covered market where you can buy the flatbread hot alongside cheese and cured meat stalls.

food.name: Strozzapreti
food.desc: Hand-rolled twists of eggless Romagnolo pasta, typically dressed with sausage ragu, tomato and a shower of squacquerone or pecorino.

places.name: Osteria de Borg
places.note: Long-running osteria in the painted fishermen's quarter; the reference point for local pasta.

places.name: Osteria del Tempo Perso
places.note: Warm, cluttered dining room doing traditional Romagnolo cooking with care.

places.name: Dalla Lella
places.note: Neighbourhood trattoria in the borgo, popular with Riminesi rather than beach crowds.

food.name: Brodetto di pesce
food.desc: Adriatic fish stew of whatever the boats landed - mantis shrimp, cuttlefish, monkfish - simmered with tomato and vinegar, mopped up with bread.

places.name: La Marianna al Lido
places.note: Long-established seafront seafood restaurant; a dependable place for the classic fish stew.

places.name: Lo Squero
places.note: Right by the canal harbour where the boats come in; straightforward Adriatic cooking.

places.name: Osteria de Borg
places.note: Traditional kitchen that cooks the sea and the countryside with equal conviction.

food.name: Sardoncini
food.desc: Small Adriatic anchovies, either grilled with breadcrumbs and rosemary or marinated in vinegar - the cheapest and best local seafood.

places.name: Lo Squero
places.note: Harbourside spot where fried and grilled small fish are the point of the menu.

places.name: Mercato Coperto fish stalls
places.note: See the morning catch, then eat it a few streets away; the market sets the day's prices.

places.name: La Marianna al Lido
places.note: Beachfront classic for fritto misto and grilled sardoncini with a glass of white.

food.name: Cappelletti in brodo
food.desc: Small hand-pinched pasta hats stuffed with soft cheese or meat, floated in a clear capon broth - the Romagnolo festive first course.

places.name: Osteria del Tempo Perso
places.note: Handmade pasta made in house; the traditional broth version appears in cooler months.

places.name: Dalla Lella
places.note: Home-style borgo trattoria where the pasta is rolled by hand daily.

places.name: Osteria de Borg
places.note: Reliable for the full canon of Romagnolo primi, cappelletti included.

food.name: Ciambella romagnola
food.desc: A dry, lightly lemony ring cake with a crunchy sugar crust, made to be dunked in sweet Albana wine at the end of a meal.

places.name: Mercato Coperto
places.note: Bakery counters sell the everyday home-style version by weight.

places.name: Osteria de Borg
places.note: Serves the ring cake with a glass of Albana as tradition demands.

places.name: Dalla Lella
places.note: Simple house desserts in the Romagnolo mould, ciambella among them.

food.name: Sangiovese di Romagna
food.desc: The hills behind Rimini make bright, cherryish Sangiovese - the everyday red poured by the carafe in every osteria.

places.name: Osteria de Borg
places.note: Good regional list including small Romagnolo growers, by the glass and carafe.

places.name: Osteria del Tempo Perso
places.note: Wine-focused osteria where the staff will steer you to a local bottle.

places.name: Borgo San Giuliano enoteche
places.note: The painted lanes across the Tiberius Bridge are lined with small wine bars.

food.name: Albana and seafront spritz
food.desc: Albana di Romagna, Italy's first white DOCG, dry or sweet - plus the ritual sunset spritz on the Rimini lungomare.

places.name: Marina Centro beach bars
places.note: The bagni turn into aperitivo bars at sunset; spritz and small bites facing the Adriatic.

places.name: Osteria del Tempo Perso
places.note: Sweet Albana served with ciambella, the correct Romagnolo way to finish dinner.

places.name: Borgo San Giuliano enoteche
places.note: Quieter, more local place for an aperitivo than the seafront strip.

landmarks: Tempio Malatestiano
Rimini's unfinished Renaissance cathedral, redesigned by Leon Battista Alberti for tyrant Sigismondo Malatesta, sheltering a Giotto crucifix and a Piero della Francesca fresco.
Ponte di Tiberio (Tiberius Bridge)
A five-arched Roman bridge of Istrian stone, completed under Tiberius in AD 21 and still carrying foot traffic over the Marecchia after two millennia.
Arco d'Augusto (Arch of Augustus)
Italy's oldest surviving Roman arch, raised in 27 BC to honour Augustus, marking the triumphant meeting point of the Via Flaminia and Via Emilia.
Borgo San Giuliano
A former fishermen's quarter of pastel lanes and murals celebrating Federico Fellini, now Rimini's most charming corner for trattorias and evening strolls.
Castel Sismondo
The brooding 15th-century fortress of Sigismondo Malatesta, its massive walls partly designed with advice from Brunelleschi and now hosting major exhibitions.
Fellini Museum
A dreamlike museum spread across Castel Sismondo and the Fulgor cinema, immersing visitors in the sets, sketches and fantasies of Rimini's great film director.
Domus del Chirurgo (Surgeon's House)
An extraordinary Roman doctor's house with vivid mosaics and the ancient world's largest surviving surgical instrument kit, excavated in Piazza Ferrari.
Piazza Cavour
Rimini's civic heart since the Middle Ages, ringed by the Palazzo dell'Arengo, the old fish market and the beloved Pigna fountain praised by Leonardo.
Piazza Tre Martiri
The ancient Roman forum where Julius Caesar reputedly addressed his troops after crossing the Rubicon, now an elegant square of clock tower and cafes.
Marina Centro Beach
The classic Riviera Romagnola strand of orderly umbrellas, beach clubs and the landmark Grand Hotel that haunted Fellini's childhood dreams.

train.note: No international trains. Rimini is on the Adriatic main line, with Frecciarossa and Italo high-speed services to Bologna in about an hour and Milan in 2h30, and regional trains down the coast to Riccione, Cattolica and Ancona. The station is a 15-minute walk from the beach and about the same from the old town. Booking opens around 120 days ahead.

bus.note: Coaches stop near the railway station. Start Romagna runs the local network including the frequent buses to San Marino, about 50 minutes inland - a genuine international hop, though no passport check applies. FlixBus handles the long-distance Italian and European routes.

ferry.note: Rimini's harbour handles fishing boats and pleasure craft, with summer excursion boats along the Riviera Romagnola but no scheduled passenger ferry. For Croatia, the crossings sail from Ancona, about 90 minutes south by train.

half.name: San Marino
half.blurb: The hilltop capital of this independent microstate lies about 40 minutes away, with a fortress and towers overlooking the surrounding countryside.

half.name: Gradara
half.blurb: A walled medieval town roughly 30 minutes away centers on a moated castle linked to the story of Paolo and Francesca in Dante's Inferno.

half.name: Urbino
half.blurb: A Renaissance hill town about an hour and 15 minutes away preserves the Ducal Palace built for Federico da Montefeltro.

half.name: Ravenna
half.blurb: A city about an hour away holds some of the best-preserved Byzantine mosaics in the world, spread across several early Christian churches and mausoleums.

half.name: San Leo
half.blurb: A fortress town roughly an hour and 10 minutes away sits atop a sheer rock outcrop and once imprisoned the occultist Cagliostro.
